topic.label: Data
topic.desc: Data work end to end: modelling and schemas, ingestion and pipelines, warehouses and analytics engineering, data quality, catalogues and lineage, exploration and visualisation, streaming, and dataset preparation for machine learning.

concepts: Designing tables and entities: normal forms, keys, dimensional models, types and evolving a schema without breaking users.
Moving data in and out: extract, load and transform jobs, scheduling, idempotent reruns, backfills and failure handling.
Querying and modelling data at scale: SQL warehouses, partitioning, incremental models, metrics definitions and cost control.
Knowing whether data can be trusted: expectations, freshness and volume checks, anomalies, missing values and reconciliation.
Finding and understanding data: catalogues, column descriptions, owners, lineage graphs and impact analysis.
Looking at data to learn from it: profiling, summaries, charts that tell the truth and sharing findings.
Event data and low-latency processing: logs, queues, windows, ordering, late events and exactly-once claims.
Preparing data for models: labelling, splits, leakage, class balance, versioning and dataset documentation.
skills: Turns a business description into entities, keys and relationships and shows the resulting tables with sample rows.
Designs fact and dimension tables for reporting questions and states the grain of each fact table.
Plans an additive or breaking schema change with a migration, a backfill and a list of downstream users.
Designs a job that extracts, transforms and loads a source, with the schedule, retries, idempotent writes and what happens on partial failure.
Checks that rerunning a job gives the same result with no duplicates and fixes steps that append blindly.
Plans a historical reload in batches, with checkpoints, cost estimate and a comparison with the old numbers.
Reads a query plan in a warehouse, finds scans and skew and rewrites the query with partition pruning or clustering.
Builds an incremental model with a unique key and a late-data window and tests it against a full rebuild.
Defines a business metric in one place with its formula, filters and owner so every report gives the same number.
Writes checks for ranges, uniqueness, nulls and allowed values, and ranks them by the harm of a failure.
Sets expected arrival time and row counts for each table and reports late or abnormal loads.
Compares totals and checksums between a source and its copy, locates the mismatched rows and explains the cause.
Writes table and column descriptions with owner and sensitivity from the data and its use, marking guesses.
Maps which tables and jobs feed each report so the reach of a change or an outage can be seen.
Lists dashboards, models and teams affected by a planned change and ranks them by how much they depend on it.
Profiles columns for types, ranges, missing values and outliers and lists the first questions the profile raises.
Chooses a chart for the question, sets axes and scales that do not mislead and writes the title as the finding.
Writes up a finding with the number, the comparison, the caveats and what decision it should or should not drive.
Designs event types with ids, timestamps and versions so streams can be ordered, deduplicated and replayed.
Builds tumbling and sliding window aggregates, handles late events with a watermark and states the delay it adds.
Checks claims of at-least-once or exactly-once delivery against how consumers actually commit and deduplicate.
Writes labelling instructions with examples and edge cases and measures how often two labellers agree.
Builds train, validation and test splits by the right unit and checks for duplicates and future information crossing them.
Documents a dataset's source, collection method, labelling process, licence, balance and known gaps in one page.
